To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the temporal evolution of the isotopic composition in cloud water can be explained by changes in the meteorological conditions during the condensation process, (2) changes in the entrained and advected vapor can also lead to changes in the isotopologues composition in cloud droplets and (3) the temporal evolution in the isotopic signature of cloud water can be used to trace the moisture source regions and to study regional recycling of moisture.
the temporal evolution of stable water isotope composition in cloud droplets was dominated by changes in local temperature or by changes in the δ values in the advected vapor.

(1) the isotopic composition in cloud droplets is sensitive to changes in meteorological parameters during condensation and (2) changes in δ values during cloud events are mainly caused by changes in meteorological properties of the advected air.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the isotopic composition in cloud water and its temporal variation in cloud droplets.
the temporal evolution of stable water isotope ratios in cloud droplets and the factors controlling this evolution.
a comprehensive study of stable isotope ratios (δ 18O and δ2H) of cloud water in a mountainous area in Germany during the Hill Cap Clouds Thuringia (HCCT- 2010) field campaign.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal evolution of the stable isotope ratios in cloud droplets depends on the interaction between the local and the regional scale.
cloud water isotopes are a sensitive tool to investigate the moisture source region of a cloud.
the isotopic composition in the cloud water is a good indicator of changes in meteorological parameters, but the isotopic composition is not a good indicator of the source region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the stable isotopic composition of cloud water is sensitive to variations in the isotopic signature of the advected vapor.

the temporal variation in the stable isotope composition in cloud droplets is mainly controlled by changes in the local meteorological conditions, whereas changes in the advected and/or entrained vapor can only be observed in case of strong variations of the meteorological conditions in the moisture source region.
the temporal changes in the stable isotope ratios in cloud water are mainly caused by the temporal changes in large scale atmospheric conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stable isotope composition in cloud droplets can serve as a proxy for the moisture history in the cloud formation region.
the isotopic composition in cloud water is a good indicator for the moisture history of the air mass.
the temporal evolution of stable isotope ratios in cloud water is highly sensitive to meteorological conditions.
